The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume the exact Planck energy and coarse entropy flux formulas of [[thm-tgr-photon-planck-flux]]. Use SI units: $G$ is in $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, $c$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $\hbar$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$, and $k_B$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. Fix a normalization of the asymptotic time and energy reference, a dimensionless fraction $0<\eta\le1$, an initial mass $M_0>0$ in kilograms, and a cutoff $0<M_{\min}<M_0$. Let $M(t)>0$ be a $C^1$ mass function on an interval containing $0$ and its first cutoff time, with $M(0)=M_0$. For each $M>0$ define the model quantities
$$r_H=\frac{2GM}{c^2},\qquad A_H=4\pi r_H^2,\qquad \kappa=\frac{c^2}{4GM},\qquad T_\infty=\frac{\hbar c\kappa}{2\pi k_B},\qquad S_B(M)=\frac{k_Bc^3A_H}{4G\hbar}+S_0.$$
Here $r_H$ is in metres, $A_H$ in square metres, $\kappa$ is the fixed-reference inverse-length parameter in inverse metres, $T_\infty$ is in kelvins, and $S_0$ is a fixed entropy offset in joules per kelvin. Adopt an effective far-field emitter with area $A_{\rm eff}=\eta A_H$ and power $P=A_{\rm eff}\sigma T_\infty^4$ in watts, where $\sigma$ is the coefficient in [[thm-tgr-photon-planck-flux]]. Adopt the mass-balance equation $c^2M'(t)=-P(t)$, with $t$ in seconds measured by the fixed asymptotic time parameter; terminate the model at the first time $M(t)=M_{\min}$. Then the exact solution until that cutoff is
$$M(t)=(M_0^3-3\alpha t)^{1/3},\qquad \alpha=\frac{\eta\hbar c^4}{15360\pi G^2},\qquad \tau=\frac{M_0^3-M_{\min}^3}{3\alpha}.$$
The parameter $\alpha$ has units $\mathrm{kg^3\,s^{-1}}$. The model exports energy $c^2(M_0-M_{\min})$ in joules through cutoff. Define its coarse exported entropy by $S_{\rm rad}(t)=\int_0^t(4/3)P(t')/T_\infty(t')\,dt'$, in joules per kelvin. Then
$$S_B(M_0)-S_B(M_{\min})>0.$$
$$S_{\rm rad}(\tau)=\frac43[S_B(M_0)-S_B(M_{\min})].$$
$$\Delta(S_B+S_{\rm rad})=\frac13[S_B(M_0)-S_B(M_{\min})]\ge0,$$
where $\Delta(S_B+S_{\rm rad})=S_B(M_{\min})+S_{\rm rad}(\tau)-S_B(M_0)$ and $S_{\rm rad}(0)=0$. This is an exact conditional calculation in the fixed-reference effective-area model. It is not a theorem about a material patch of a null horizon, an exact time-dependent Einstein solution, quantum backreaction, reference-independent Stefan emission, or a universal generalized second law.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as defined by [[def-countable-choice]] and use the fixed-reference mathematical emitter model of [[prop-tgr-ideal-evaporation-accounting]], with positive constants $G,c$, a positive mass function $M(t_\infty)$, and the model horizon radius $r_H(M)=2GM/c^2$. Here $t_\infty$ is measured in seconds, $M$ in kilograms, $r_H$ in metres, $G$ in $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, and $c$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. At each $t_\infty$ before the positive-mass cutoff, define the selected crossing-time scale and dimensionless fractional-change diagnostic by

$$ t_{\mathrm{cross}}(t_\infty):=\frac{r_H(M(t_\infty))}{c}, \qquad \epsilon_{\mathrm{qs}}(t_\infty):=\frac{|M'(t_\infty)|\,t_{\mathrm{cross}}(t_\infty)}{M(t_\infty)}. $$

Thus $t_{\mathrm{cross}}$ has units of seconds and $\epsilon_{\mathrm{qs}}$ is dimensionless. This is a diagnostic defined from the adopted mass ODE and the chosen length scale $r_H/c$; it is not a measured crossing time, an estimate of error against a time-dependent Einstein solution, or a proof that the ideal model approximates such a solution.

Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$ and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be
continuous on $[a,b]$ ([[def-continuity-real]], [[def-interval]]) and
differentiable at every point of $(a,b)$ as a function on $[a,b]$
([[def-derivative]]). Then there is $c \in (a,b)$ with

$$f(b) - f(a) \;=\; f'(c)\,(b - a) .$$

Equivalently, since $b - a \ne 0$, there is $c \in (a,b)$ at which
$f'(c) = \bigl(f(b)-f(a)\bigr)/(b-a)$: the derivative somewhere inside equals
the average rate of change across the whole interval.

**Continuity on the closed interval cannot be dropped.** Differentiability at
every point of $(a,b)$ alone does not suffice: a function on $[0,1]$,
differentiable at every point of $(0,1)$ with derivative constantly $1$, for
which no $c$ works, is exhibited later on this page as a false statement, and
the companion page works the same witness out in full.

derivations.claim:
Differentiate the exact solution in [F1] on $0\leq t_\infty\leq\tau$; since $M(t_\infty)>0$, this gives $M'=-\alpha/M^2$. Also [F1] gives $r_H=2GM/c^2$, so substituting these identities and $t_{\mathrm{cross}}=r_H/c$ into [F2] yields
$$
\epsilon_{\mathrm{qs}}=\frac{(\alpha/M^2)(2GM/c^3)}{M} =\frac{2G\alpha}{c^3M^2}.
$$
All factors are positive on the interval.
From [F1], $M(t_\infty+\Delta t)^3=M(t_\infty)^3-3\alpha\Delta t$. Divide by the positive $M(t_\infty)^3$ and take positive cube roots to get $M(t_\infty+\Delta t)/M(t_\infty)=(1-\delta)^{1/3}$.

Since $M(t_\infty)\geq M_{\min}>0$, one has $M(t_\infty)^{-2}\leq M_{\min}^{-2}$. The formula in step 1.1 gives the uniform upper bound; if $M_{\min}^2\geq2G\alpha/(c^3\epsilon_0)$, multiplying by the positive denominator yields $\epsilon_{\mathrm{qs}}\leq\epsilon_0$.

If $\delta=0$, step 1.2 gives a ratio of one and the bound is equality. If $0<\delta\leq1/2$, $h(x)=(1-x)^{1/3}$ is continuous on $[0,\delta]$, differentiable on its interior, and satisfies $|h'(x)|=\frac13(1-x)^{-2/3}\leq2^{2/3}/3$. Apply [F3] on this nondegenerate interval and use $h(0)=1$ to obtain $|h(\delta)-1|\leq(2^{2/3}/3)\delta$. Step 1.2 gives the claimed ratio bound.

$$
r_H(M)=2m=\frac{2G_NM}{c^2},\qquad A_H(M)=4\pi r_H(M)^2,\qquad \kappa_{\rm geom}(M)=\frac{1}{4m}=\frac{c^2}{4G_NM}.

The effective area is not a material patch of the null horizon and $\eta$ is not a frequency-independent greybody factor applied separately to entropy.

The model holds only for the fixed normalization $\xi$. No experiment, coupled backreaction solution, physical extinction event, or universal generalized second law is adopted.

Fix $L,T,\hbar,c,k_B>0$ with SI units respectively metre, kelvin, joule-second, metre per second, and joule per kelvin. Let $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ in inverse joules. Let $\Omega_B$ be the finite-support maps $m:I\to\mathbb N_0$, set $E(m)=\sum_{i\in I}\epsilon_i m_i$, and let $\mathcal H_B=\ell^2(\Omega_B,\mathbb C)$ with its occupation basis. Define the nonnegative diagonal multiplier $H$ by $(Ha)_m=E(m)a_m$ on $D(H)=\{a\in\ell^2(\Omega_B,\mathbb C):\sum_m E(m)^2|a_m|^2<\infty\}$, so $H|m\rangle=E(m)|m\rangle$. Set $q_n=e^{-\beta\epsilon_{(n,1)}}$, $Z_L=Z_L(\beta)$, $\rho_L=Z_L^{-1}e^{-\beta H}$, and $p_m=e^{-\beta E(m)}/Z_L$. Define the diagonal-state entropy by $S_L=-k_B\sum_{m\in\Omega_B}p_m\log p_m$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm.

The finite-box trace, energy and entropy are actual diagonal sums, not continuum mode integrals. The partition function $Z_L$ and occupations $q_n$ are dimensionless, $\rho_L$ has trace one, energy and $U_L$ have units joules, and $S_L$ has units joules per kelvin. The sums satisfy $Z_L=\prod_{n\ne0}(1-q_n)^{-2}<\infty$, $\rho_L$ is a positive trace-one trace-class operator, and every nonnegative integer energy moment under $\rho_L$ is finite. Moreover,
$$U_L=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_LH)=2\sum_{n\ne0}\frac{\epsilon_{(n,1)}}{e^{\beta\epsilon_{(n,1)}}-1}<\infty.$$
The entropy is
$$S_L=k_B(\log Z_L+\beta U_L)=2k_B\sum_{n\ne0}\left[-\log(1-q_n)+\frac{\beta\epsilon_{(n,1)}q_n}{1-q_n}\right]<\infty.$$

$$\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{2}{L^3}\sum_{n\ne0}\frac{\hbar\omega_n}{e^{\beta\hbar\omega_n}-1}\psi(\omega_n)=\frac{\hbar}{\pi^2c^3}\int_0^\infty\frac{\omega^3\psi(\omega)}{e^{\beta\hbar\omega}-1}\,d\omega.$$
The integrated limits are
$$u=\lim_{L\to\infty}u_L=\frac{\pi^2k_B^4T^4}{15\hbar^3c^3},\qquad s=\lim_{L\to\infty}s_L=\frac{4u}{3T}.$$

Define one-sided flux through a plane by integrating the outward normal velocity component over the outward hemisphere. The hypotheses of [F3] match the fixed-reference area, temperature, outgoing flux, mass-balance law, and strictly positive cutoff in [F1]. Its exact solution gives the displayed $M(t_\infty)$, $\tau$, and energy export. No continuation to $M=0$ is used.

Therefore [L1] gives $S_H(M)=k_Bc^3A_H(M)/(4G_N\hbar)+s_*$, while [F3] gives $S_B(M)=k_Bc^3A_H(M)/(4G_N\hbar)+S_0$. Their constant offsets may differ, but subtracting the values at $M_0$ and $M_{\min}$ cancels each offset and gives $S_H(M_0)-S_H(M_{\min})=S_B(M_0)-S_B(M_{\min})>0$, because $M_0>M_{\min}>0$. The $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ assumption [A2] is carried for the reduced-spectrum input in [L1].

The definition [F4] and ODE of [F3] give $\epsilon_{\rm qs}=|M'|(2G_NM/c^3)/M=2G_N\alpha/(c^3M^2)$. Since $M\geq M_{\min}$, the supremum is the displayed positive-cutoff value; the threshold follows by multiplying by $M_{\min}^2>0$. The exact finite-interval ratio and bound are [F5]. These are internal properties of the stipulated ODE.

By [F3], $S_{\rm rad}(\tau)=(4/3)[S_B(M_0)-S_B(M_{\min})]$. Step 1.3 replaces this difference by $\Delta S_H$. Thus $S_{\rm rad}(\tau)=(4/3)\Delta S_H$, and $S_H(M_{\min})+S_{\rm rad}(\tau)-S_H(M_0)=-(\Delta S_H)+(4/3)\Delta S_H=(1/3)\Delta S_H>0$. This is the stated coarse model entropy accounting only.

Under the rescaling $\xi_b=b\xi$, the energy $E_\xi=-c\,p_a\xi^a$ scales by $b$, the normalized time parameter scales as $t_b=t_\infty/b$, and the geometric surface gravity scales as $\kappa_b=b\kappa_{\rm geom}$. Hence $P_b=dE_b/dt_b=b^2P_\infty$, while $T_b=\hbar c\kappa_b/(2\pi k_B)=bT_\infty$, so $A_{\rm eff}\sigma T_b^4=b^4A_{\rm eff}\sigma T_\infty^4$ with unchanged area and coefficient. The equality stipulated in [F1] therefore belongs to its fixed normalization and cannot be reused unchanged for arbitrary $b$.

citations.quote:
Assume the ideal model and fixed asymptotic normalization of [[post-tgr-photon-emitter-and-quasistatic-balance]], and explicitly assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as defined by [[def-countable-choice]]. Use $G=G_N$ between the mathematical ODE input and the physical Schwarzschild family. Also assume the conditional family-entropy interface stated by [[pthm-tgr-area-entropy-calibration]] with its actual hypotheses. Let $S_H(M)$ denote that state-function value at the stationary Schwarzschild member of mass $M$, and put
$$
\Delta S_H:=S_H(M_0)-S_H(M_{\min}).
$$
For the fixed-reference effective-area model,
$$
P_\infty(M)=\frac{\eta\hbar c^6}{15360\pi G_N^2M^2}, \qquad \alpha=\frac{\eta\hbar c^4}{15360\pi G_N^2}, \qquad M(t_\infty)=(M_0^3-3\alpha t_\infty)^{1/3}, \qquad \tau=\frac{M_0^3-M_{\min}^3}{3\alpha}.
$$
The model exports energy $c^2(M_0-M_{\min})$ joules, and its coarse photon entropy satisfies
$$
S_H(M)=\frac{4\pi k_BG_NM^2}{\hbar c}+s_*, \qquad s_*\in\mathbb R\ \text{constant on the stationary family},
$$
$$
S_{\rm rad}(\tau)=\frac43\Delta S_H>0, \qquad \Delta(S_H+S_{\rm rad})=\frac13\Delta S_H>0.
$$
The absolute entropy offsets in the mathematical ODE model and the stationary-family state function need not be identified; their differences agree because both have the same area coefficient on this branch.

For the diagnostic of [[def-tgr-emitter-quasistatic-diagnostic]],
$$
\epsilon_{\rm qs}(t_\infty)=\frac{2G_N\alpha}{c^3M(t_\infty)^2}, \qquad \sup_{0\leq t_\infty\leq\tau}\epsilon_{\rm qs} =\frac{2G_N\alpha}{c^3M_{\min}^2}.
$$
Thus $M_{\min}^2\geq2G_N\alpha/(c^3\epsilon_0)$ implies $\epsilon_{\rm qs}\leq\epsilon_0$ for any $\epsilon_0>0$. The finite-interval bound in [[lem-tgr-emitter-quasistatic-bounds]] also applies whenever its stated $\delta\leq1/2$ condition holds.

The Stefan closure is tied to the fixed reference: under $\xi\mapsto b\xi$, power scales as $b^2$, while $T_\xi^4$ scales as $b^4$ and area is unchanged. This is an exact conditional model calculation, not a Hawking-radiation theorem, a time-dependent Einstein solution, a backreaction error estimate, an observed evaporation history, or a universal generalized second law.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim:
With $\eta=1$, [F1] gives $\alpha=\hbar c^4/(15360\pi G_N^2)$. Hence $t_*=M_0^3/(3\alpha)=5120\pi G_N^2M_0^3/(\hbar c^4)$, and
$$
\tau=\frac{M_0^3-(M_0/2)^3}{3\alpha} =\left(1-\frac18\right)t_*=\frac78t_*.
$$
The cutoff remains positive, $M(\tau)=M_0/2$, so the model does not reach its algebraic zero-mass time.
The energy export in [F1] is $c^2(M_0-M_{\min})$. Substituting [A1] gives $c^2M_0/2$ joules.

By [F1], $S_H(M)=4\pi k_BG_NM^2/(\hbar c)+s_*$ on the selected branch, with an unfixed constant $s_*$. Subtracting its values at $M_0$ and $M_0/2$ cancels $s_*$ and gives $\Delta S_H=4\pi k_BG_N(3M_0^2/4)/(\hbar c)=3\pi k_BG_NM_0^2/(\hbar c)$. The entropy export is $4\Delta S_H/3=4\pi k_BG_NM_0^2/(\hbar c)$, and the total gain is $\Delta S_H/3=\pi k_BG_NM_0^2/(\hbar c)$.

The maximum diagnostic occurs at $M=M_{\min}=M_0/2$, so [F1] gives
$$
\epsilon_{\rm qs,max}=\frac{2G_N\alpha}{c^3(M_0/2)^2} =\frac{8G_N\alpha}{c^3M_0^2} =\frac{\hbar c}{1920\pi G_NM_0^2}.
$$
The displayed lower bound on $M_0^2$ is equivalent, after multiplication by the positive $1920\pi G_NM_0^2\epsilon_0/(\hbar c)$, to $\epsilon_{\rm qs,max}\leq\epsilon_0$. This remains an internal diagnostic for the stipulated ODE, not a comparison with a coupled spacetime solution.
